Part A:
- Principal $P = 12000$
- Monthly interest rate $r = 0.069 / 12 = 0.00575$
- Total months $n = 60$
- Standard monthly payment $M = P \frac{r(1+r)^n}{(1+r)^n - 1}$:
  $M = 12000 \times \frac{0.00575(1.00575)^{60}}{(1.00575)^{60} - 1} \approx 237.070659$
- Let $B_k$ be the balance after month $k$. Without extra payments, $B_k = P(1+r)^k - M \frac{(1+r)^k - 1}{r}$.
- With extra payments of $E_4 = 500$ at month 4 and $E_8 = 600$ at month 8:
  Balance at month 18:
  $B_{18} = P(1+r)^{18} - M \frac{(1+r)^{18}-1}{r} - E_4(1+r)^{14} - E_8(1+r)^{10}$
  - $(1+r) = 1.00575$
  - $(1+r)^{18} \approx 1.10862025$
  - Regular balance at month 18: $12000 \times (1.00575)^{18} - 237.070659 \times \frac{(1.00575)^{18} - 1}{0.00575} \approx 13303.443 - 4478.471 = 8824.972$
  - Extra payment deductions:

    $600 \times (1.00575)^{10} \approx 600 \times 1.0590059 = 635.4035$
  - Remaining balance: $8824.972 - 541.767 - 635.404 \approx 7647.8016 \approx 7647.80$

Part B:

- Sequence of multipliers:

  $P_0 \times 0.9 \times 1.2 \times 0.85 \times 1.2 \times 1.18 = 97.50$

Part C:
- System of congruences:
  $x \equiv 15 \pmod{19} \implies x \equiv -4 \pmod{19}$
  $x \equiv 5 \pmod{23}$
  $x \equiv 2 \pmod{17}$
- From $x \equiv 5 \pmod{23}$: $x = 23k + 5$
- Modulo 19:
  $23k + 5 \equiv 4k + 5 \equiv 15 \implies 4k \equiv 10 \equiv 29 \equiv 48 \implies k \equiv 12 \pmod{19}$
  $x = 23(19m + 12) + 5 = 437m + 281$
- Modulo 17:
  $437 \equiv 12 \pmod{17}$
  $281 \equiv 9 \pmod{17}$
  $12m + 9 \equiv 2 \pmod{17} \implies 12m \equiv -7 \equiv 10 \pmod{17}$
  Multiply by $12^{-1} \equiv 7 \pmod{17}$ (since $12 \times 7 = 84 \equiv -1 \implies 12^{-1} = 10$):
  $12 \times 10 = 120 = 7 \times 17 + 1 \implies 12^{-1} \equiv 10$.
  $m \equiv 10 \times 10 = 100 \equiv 15 \pmod{17}$.
- Smallest positive integer corresponds to $m = 15$:
  $x = 437 \times 15 + 281 = 6555 + 281 = 6836$.
